question.text: Under GAAR provisions (effective 1 April 2017), an arrangement can be declared 'impermissible avoidance' only if its MAIN PURPOSE is to obtain a tax benefit AND it satisfies at least one of four tainted elements. Which of the following is NOT one of the four tainted elements per Chapter 14?

answer.text: Creates rights/obligations not ordinarily created between arm's-length parties
Results in direct or indirect misuse or abuse of the ITA
Has an aggregate tax benefit of less than INR 3 crore
Lacks commercial substance in whole or in part

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The four tainted elements are: (i) non-arm's-length rights/obligations, (ii) misuse/abuse of the ITA, (iii) lacks commercial substance, (iv) not normally employed for bona-fide purposes. The INR 3 crore threshold (the workbook actually cites INR 30 million = 3 cr as the DE MINIMIS exemption) is a MONETARY filter, not a tainted element. Also CBDT has clarified the limit is per-arrangement, not per-taxpayer. **The Trap:** A, B, D are all verbatim tainted elements. C looks plausible because GAAR has a INR 3 cr de minimis, but that is a threshold, not a tainted element. **Cross-Exam Context:** X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) tests GAAR tainted elements at client-planning level. XIX-E tests it for fund-structure compliance. XXIV (AML) overlaps at the commercial-substance analysis. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When Nilgiri considers a Mauritius feeder to funnel NR capital, document commercial substance BEYOND tax — local director, board meetings in Port Louis, operational expenses. GAAR + MLI PPT will dissect the structure; mere LOB satisfaction is necessary but not sufficient.
